Date January 22, 1940.
Subject. Japanese Authorities contemplating control of bricks and tiles
business.
Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tee Liang Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the press report (attached)
stating that the Japanese authorities are contemplating
control of the trade in bricks and tiles, discreet
enquiries ascertain the these authorities commenced
interfering with the transportation of bricks and
tiles to Shanghai on December 25, 1939.
The principal source of this building material
is Kashan (Chekiang Province), and transport to
Shanghai is done by boats. On December 25, 1939,
consignments, on their way to Shanghai, were detained
by the Japanese authorities near No. 34 Bridge on the
Shanghai-Hangchow railway line to the south of
Sungkiang, when the dealers were told that these
materials were required by the Japanese military.
The tiles and bricks detained were later bought by
the authorities concerned at the following prices :-
Bricks: - $85 to $90 per 10,000 pieces.
Tiles :Old style - $45 to $50 per 10,000 "
New style - $60 to $70 per 1,000 "
In consequence of the detention, the majority of the
dealers temporarily suspended transporting tiles and
bricks to Shanghai because of a fear of further
interference. However occasional supplies have
succeeded in reaching Shanghai from time to time
through assistance by Japanese subjects, but in this
way extra expenses amounting to $200 per junk load
are incurred, thus increasing the prices locally.

制作人：刑事侦缉督察 Sih Tee Liang 转呈人：侦探督察 Crawford

鉴于（附后）新闻报道指出日本当局正考虑控制砖瓦贸易，经谨慎查询查明，这些当局自1939年12月25日起开始干扰向上海运输砖瓦。
该建筑材料的主要来源是嘉兴（浙江省），运往上海系通过船只进行。1939年12月25日，在运往上海的途中，几批货物在松江以南的沪杭铁路34号桥附近被日本当局扣留，当时商人被告知日军需要这些材料。
被扣留的瓦片和砖块后来被有关当局以以下价格购买：
砖块：每10,000块85至90美元。
瓦片：旧式——每10,000块45至50美元；
新式——每1,000块60至70美元。
由于此次扣留，大多数商人因担心进一步干扰而暂时停止向上海运输瓦片和砖块。然而，偶尔仍有供应在日本人的协助下成功运抵上海，但这种方式导致每船额外增加200美元的费用，从而推高了本地价格。

January 17. 1940.                                          Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wen Pao, National Herald 1-
JAPANESE AUTHORITIES CONTEMPLATING CONTROL OF
BRICKS AND TILES BUSINESS

The Japanese economic aggression of China
is so severe that sales of rice, wheat, cotton, carbon,
lumber, fruits, field products and vegetables are all
controlled by the Japanese authorities, who have lately
been contemplating the control of bricks and tiles and
other construction materials.
According to enquiries made by our reporter
yesterday from responsible sources, recently certain
local unscrupulous elements have been making endeavours
to negotiate with the Japanese authorities to obtain a
promise of security by payment of a considerable amount
of money in order to satisfy the Japanese concerned.
It is learned that members of the local
Bricks and Tiles Trade Guild have expressed their non-
co-operation in this matter and they will also voice a
strong objection.

日本对中国的经济侵略如此严重，以至于大米、小麦、棉花、煤炭、木材、水果、农产品和蔬菜的销售均受日本当局控制，他们最近一直在考虑控制砖瓦和其他建筑材料。
据本报记者昨日从可靠消息源获悉，近期当地某些不法分子一直试图与日本当局谈判，通过支付巨额款项以获得安全承诺，从而取悦相关日方人员。
据悉，当地砖瓦同业公会成员已表示在此事上不予合作，并将提出强烈反对。

“所有第三国包装公司必须停止购买鸡蛋，并停止干涉日本在中国的经济发展。”
这是日本组织亚洲开发委员会向在上海从事鸡蛋业务的两家美国公司和五家英国公司中的一家作出的惊人声明。
另一家公司已收到三井物产株式会社的通知，该会社已窃取了这七家公司付款购买的价值五十万美元的鸡蛋，通知称这些公司必须停止购买鸡蛋，因为鸡蛋贸易必须处于 MBK 的控制之下。
更多阻碍
据报道，日本人采取了进一步的阻碍策略，以阻止这七家公司提取在三角洲地区购买的鸡蛋，因为亚洲开发委员会现在要求对运抵上海的货物出具“提货许可证”。
此类许可证曾在实际装运鸡蛋时由日本人在长江沿线的一些航运港口签发，但目前使用的一些装运点并不签发这些许可证。结果是，亚洲开发委员会索要从未签发过的许可证，目前约有2000篮鸡蛋滞留在北站，这七家公司无法提取这批易腐货物。
阻遏策略
这些公司指出，在对价值五十万美元的货物进行大规模抢劫之后，随之而来的是旨在阻遏第三国公司继续从事鸡蛋贸易的策略。它们中的大多数实际上已暂停业务，但仍购买少量鸡蛋货物以勉强维持运营，以此努力抵抗恐吓。
尽管日本宣布希望改善与这两个国家的关系，但驻上海领事们的多次抗议并未阻止 MBK 试图从美英公司手中窃取整个贸易。已向驻东京大使馆提交报告，此事正在那里审议，但与此同时，日本人在上海的侵略性策略仍在继续。

Costumes Only Needed
If the ADC would wish to put
on the Pirates of Penzance, all
they'd have to do is get together
the costumes. We know where
they could get a perfect cast—even
if it is a modern one.
And so back to the egg busi-
ness. It's one of those big enter-
prises in China, with Chinese,
Japanese, British and American
commercial houses all engaged in
the trade. They've been carrying
on for years.
That "Open Door"
But now the picture is changed.
Once upon a time the Yangtze
River was wide and its waters
flowed free for vessels of all na-
tions. Then the Yangtze, like a
few other things connected with
the pertinent "Open Door" ques-
tion, became closed—except for
one nation. They could afford an
army to do it with.
Nowadays if a firm wants to
continue its business upriver, it
can only use Japanese ships.
Other vessels could sail on those
same waters, too, but their Powers
won't let them. So they don't.
So the story comes back in
particular, to the egg dealing
firms, British and American, who
must get the product. They use
Japanese vessels. In return they
obtain a bill of lading, which con-
tains the "marks" of the British
or American firm.
The "Consignee"
But at the bottom of the bill of
lading is a short dotted line which
is led off by the word "consignee."
The Mitsui Bussan Kaisha chooses
to have its name placed there and,
because there is no other alter-
native, the British and American
firms have to tolerate this un-
orthodox practice.
Still the eggs are not delivered
to their rightful owners. Who,
asks the MBK, when they are
asked for the eggs, yes who are
the consignees? You British and
American firms, can't you read
your own language? Doesn't it
say 'Mitsui Bussan Kaisha?'
It says Mitsui Bussan Kaisha,
alright. And it says, too, that the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha is taking
things which do not belong to the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.
Not One Denial
More than that, the return of
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha which
is a fully-recognized Japanese
firm, to illegal practices which it
has so far failed to deny in the
least as being reflects on prestige
and honor.
The Evening Post learned this
morning that following the re-
newal of the MBK's tactics in
seizing cargoes of eggs belonging
to British and American firms,
both the American British Con-
sulates here took up vigorous in-
vestigation and are likely to lodge
firm protests with the Japanese
authorities.
Reports received in Shanghai
this morning revealed that Chin-
ese farmers in Japanese-occupied
areas, particularly in Wusih, were
ordered to sell eggs only to Ja-
panese—and at a much lower
price than that offered them by
British and American egg dealers.

只需戏服
如果副官想上演《彭赞斯的海盗》，他们所要做的只是凑齐戏服。我们知道哪里可以找到完美的演员阵容——即使是现代版的。
回到鸡蛋业务上来。这是中国的大型企业之一，中国、日本、英国和美国的商号都参与其中。这项贸易已持续多年。
那扇“开放门户”
但现在情况发生了变化。曾几何时，长江宽阔，其水域对所有国家的船只自由开放。后来，长江以及与相关的“门户开放”问题有关的其他一些事物一样，变得封闭了——除了对一个国家例外。他们负担得起一支军队来做到这一点。
如今，如果一家公司想继续其在长江上游的业务，它只能使用日本船只。其他船只也可以在这些水域航行，但其所属强国不允许它们这样做。所以它们就不去了。
因此，故事具体回到了必须获取产品的英美鸡蛋交易公司身上。它们使用日本船只。作为回报，它们获得了一份提单，其中包含该英国或美国公司的“标记”。
“收货人”
但在提单的底部有一条短虚线，由“consignee”（收货人）一词引出。三井物产株式会社选择将其名称放在那里，并且由于没有其他选择，英美公司不得不容忍这种非正统的做法。
然而，鸡蛋并未交付给其合法所有者。当被要求交付鸡蛋时，MBK 问道，谁是收货人？你们这些英美公司，难道看不懂自己的语言吗？上面不是写着‘三井物产株式会社’吗？
上面确实写着三井物产株式会社。但也表明，三井物产株式会社正在拿走不属于三井物产株式会社的东西。
无一否认
不仅如此，三井物产株式会社作为一家得到充分认可的日本公司，回归非法行径，且至今未能对此作出丝毫否认，这反映了其声望和荣誉问题。
《晚邮报》今晨获悉，继 MBK 再次采取手段扣押属于英美公司的鸡蛋货物后，驻此地的美国和英国领事馆均展开了 vigorous 调查，并可能向日本当局提出坚决抗议。
今晨在上海收到的报告显示，日军占领区（特别是无锡）的中国农民被命令只将鸡蛋卖给日本人——且价格远低于英美鸡蛋经销商向他们提供的价格。

Chinese-American Daily News, Hwa Pao, Ta Mei Pao, Sin Wan

JAPANESE AND THE PORK BUSINESS

In spring this year a Livestock Market was
inaugurated in Hongkew under the auspices of the Asia
Development Board. When this market began to exercise
control over the local pork trade, a strike of pork shops
resulted as a protest against this control. However,
owing to existing conditions in Shanghai, the pork shops,
with a view to preserving their business and to supply
the requirements of the public, had to resume operations,
although their trade would be under the control of the
Japanese and the City Government authorities.
On November 2 the Livestock Market was
re-organized because of intense dissensions. A Japanese
named Matsuishi was appointed by the Japanese authorities
and one Chia (贾) was appointed by the City Government
as responsible officials of the market. Being
unfamiliar with the pork trade, these two men, at the
instigation of speculators and profiteers, recklessly
raised the prices at the auctions, with the result that
the market became highly confused and the price of pork
was considerably increased. It is learned that for
a pig transported from Kiangpeh to the Foreign Settlements,
the buyer has to pay about $20 in commissions to the
Livestock Market and other taxes.
Owing to the excessively high price of pork,
the consumption of pork in Shanghai has considerably
decreased as compared with a daily consumption of some
3,000 pigs in former times.

日本人与猪肉业

今年春季，在亚洲开发委员会的主持下，虹口成立了一个牲畜市场。当该市场开始对当地猪肉贸易实施控制时，肉铺罢工以示抗议。然而，鉴于上海的现有状况，肉铺为了维持生意并满足公众需求，不得不恢复营业，尽管其贸易将处于日本人和市政府当局的控制之下。
11月2日，由于激烈的分歧，牲畜市场进行了重组。一名名叫 Matsuishi（音译）的日本人被日本当局任命，一名姓贾（Chia）的人被市政府任命为市场的负责人。由于不熟悉猪肉贸易，这两人在投机者和奸商的唆使下，在拍卖中肆意抬高价格，导致市场极度混乱，猪肉价格大幅上涨。据悉，一头从闸北运往公共租界的猪，买家需向牲畜市场支付约20美元的佣金及其他税费。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

NOV 1 4 1939

Japanese Control
Match Industry
Shortage of Materials as
Result of War Gives Them
Virtual Monopoly

While it is impossible now for
Chinese merchants to buy raw mater-
ials for making matches from Europ-
ean countries now engaged in war,
the Japanese have now practically
monopolized the industry to such an
extent that the supply and distribu-
tion of matches in this country are
virtually a Japanese business, Chinese
reports indicate. The only match
manufacturing factory that is not
controlled by the Japanese is an
American firm in Shanghai.
Since the outbreak of hostilities in
Europe, Chinese match manufactur-
ers have been dependent on Japan
for the supply of all raw materials,
and making full use of the situation,
the Japanese have limited the supply
of the materials to individual Chinese
factories, it is asserted. Prices have
been increased considerably and the
Chinese are forced to sell the goods
at high prices. Meanwhile, the re-
ports say, Japanese match manu-
facturing factories in Tsingtao and
Tientsin have been encouraged to ac-
celerate their efficiency.
The reports explain that the Japan-
ese had planned for the control of
the Chinese match industry even be-
fore the outbreak of Sino-Japanese
hostilities. They once proposed to
the Chinese to organize a joint sales
office but the request was turned
down. Since the war, all Chinese
match manufacturing factories in oc-
cupied districts have been forced to
participate in the "National Joint
Office of the Match Business of
China" which has its head office in
Tientsin.
A branch of this office was estab-
lished in Shanghai in July of this
year, about two months before the
outbreak of war in Europe. Those
in charge of the branch have been
supervising the production of matches
here by giving certificates. Only
after these certificates have been
obtained can Chinese match manu-
facturers distribute their cargo
freely, it is stated.

《字林西报》。

1939年11月14日

日本控制
火柴工业
战争导致的材料短缺
使他们获得事实上的垄断

虽然中国商人现在无法从正处于战争状态的欧洲国家购买制造火柴的原材料，但据中文报道显示，日本人现在实际上已经垄断了该行业，以至于本国的火柴供应和分销 virtually 成为日本的生意。唯一不受日本人控制的火柴制造厂是上海的一家美国公司。
自欧洲敌对行动爆发以来，中国火柴制造商一直依赖日本供应所有原材料，据称，日本人充分利用这一局势，限制了对个别中国工厂的材料供应。价格大幅提高，中国人被迫以高价出售商品。同时，报道说，青岛和天津的日本火柴制造厂被鼓励提高效率。
报道解释说，日本人在中日敌对行动爆发之前就计划控制中国火柴工业。他们曾向中方提议组建一个联合销售办事处，但该请求被拒绝。自战争爆发以来，占领区的所有中国火柴制造厂都被迫参加总部设在天津的“中华火柴业全国联合办事处”。
该办事处的一个分支于今年7月在上海成立，大约在欧洲战争爆发前两个月。负责该分支的人员一直通过颁发证书来监督这里的火柴生产。据说，只有获得这些证书后，中国火柴制造商才能自由分销其货物。

At 2.15 p.m. July 15, 1938, the Private Indian Watchman employed at the Mei Foong (美丰) Textile Coy's Factory at 750 Kungping Road reported by telephone that number of Japanese had entered the factory and had placed a notice on the main gate.

Inspt. Palmer Officer i/c, Sub-Inspt. Nakano and D.S. Suhoff proceeded to the scene and ascertained that this factory was being taken over by a Mr. M. Tokuchin (Tokuchin Yoko), Lane 180 House 332 Woosung Road Telephone No.42796. Mr. Tokuchin produced documents from the Japanese Consulate, Japanese Naval Landing Party and Military Gendarmerie authorizing him to take over the premises at 750 Kungping Road.

A Japanese flag has been hoisted over the main gate besides a board with a notice in Japanese.

Mr. Tokuchin informed Police that he intended commencing work on the morrow with about three hundred employees.

Police informed the Japanese that this mill was under British management. Not being in possession of any documentary evidence however the police could not take any further action.

Mr. Golding, who is at present ill, was informed by telephone (No. 38096) of the entry. He is endeavouring to get copies of registration etc. from H.B.M. Consulate and at the same time lodge a protest.

Sir,
At 3.40 p.m. July 14, 1938, Mr. Golding with office address at 2J Canton Road, General Manager of the Mei Foong (美豐) Textile Coy., with offices at 207 Tientsin Road, came to the Station and reported that his Indian Watchman had telephoned him to the effect that two Japanese civilians had entered the Factory premises at 750 Kungping Road.
D.S. Suhoff, J.P.C.2 and the undersigned proceeded to the Factory with Mr. Golding but discovered the Japanese had already left.
The Indian Watchman stated that the Japanese had entered, inspected the factory, gaining entry to a godown by breaking a pad-lock from the door. They informed the Indian Watchman they, Japanese, were going to open the mill and would return on the morrow.
Watchman instructed to telephone Mr. Golding and Police Station should these men reappear.
It may be noted that this factory was originally a Chinese concern according to Factory List but owing to some financial difficulties, date of which are not at present known, the whole concern was mortgaged to the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation. It is from this Bank the present company are taking over the mill under British management and are endeavouring to open up for business in a week or so.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

THE DISPUTE ABOUT BRITISH MILLS

THE dispute between the Japanese authorities and the owners of two British cotton mills headed by Mr. W. C. Gomersall is attracting wide attention and interest because its outcome may have far-reaching effect on all foreign property in the Japanese-occupied areas, and on the high seas.

The two mills in question, originally registered as Chinese were bought by the British interests represented by Mr. Gomersall after the outbreak of hostilities. Subsequently, the mills were taken over by the Japanese upon order of their military and it is alleged that certain members detailed by the owners to look after the premises were ejected at the threat of arrest.

Extraordinary meetings of the British owners were called, and much indignation was expressed by their directors. Official action has been and is being taken through the British Consulate-General to effect the return of the property to their lawful owners, and to date the Japanese authorities have not seen fit to acquiesce in the British demand.

The position taken by the Japanese military in the first instance was based upon a public notice issued sometime in September last, in which transactions between the Chinese and foreign nationals concerning property of any kind consummated after the outbreak of the war, whether genuine or fictitious, would not be recognized by the Japanese authorities.

The position, as pointed out in these columns previously, is too unilateral to be tenable in international law or according to international usage. The operation of military hostilities between two nations does not preclude the possibility of trade between nationals of either with those of a third nation provided, of course, that such trade does not include contraband.

In fact, the continuance of hostilities cannot but provide excellent opportunities to purchase property at bargain prices, and this is all good business pure and simple.

In China, this principle is further reinforced by the fact that foreign nationals, with a few exceptions, have concentrated most of their property holdings within the International Settlement and the French Concession, both of which are immune from the operation of war by virtue of their international or foreign national character. In both areas the Chinese and Japanese are free to reside and trade, and surely it must follow that other foreign nationals must enjoy the same privilege to deal with either the Chinese or the Japanese in normal trade and commerce.

The fallacy in the position assumed by the Japanese appears to have impressed itself upon the Japanese consular officials. Thus, as reported, the Japanese spokesman in connection with this dispute has stated that the fact that the mills were transferred after the outbreak of the hostilities is of “secondary importance”.

The only point on which the Japanese are now insisting is the bona fide British ownership of the two mills involved. Though it may appear a simple matter to prove one’s ownership, it is in fact most difficult in the circumstance.

What the Japanese may demand as proof of ownership may be much more than what is usually required by a court of law. The British owners have already submitted all the documents for this purpose to the British Consulate-General which has in turn submitted them to the Japanese Consulate-General and finally the Japanese military commander.

The attitude of the British owners is that official certification of British ownership by the British Consulate-General should suffice while the Japanese are apparently demanding something more than mere British official registration.

While it may be admitted that not all official registration papers are absolute proof of genuine ownership because even officials may be fallible or gullible unwittingly, yet international comity dictates the acceptance by the representative of one nation of an official statement from the representative of another nation in normal course of events. The world would indeed become a spectre of unbelievable conclusion if each nation were free, at its own whim and fancy, to require the minutest detail of private ownership besides official certification. In Shanghai alone the Japanese authorities would have their hands full if they were to take it upon themselves to prove or disprove foreign ownership of property instead of relying upon the good faith of officials of other Powers. International comity is not only a matter of diplomatic amenities but also the result of centuries of hard experience.

The trouble which has developed from the present dispute, if not promptly adjusted, may cost the Japanese more in the way of goodwill and business than the retention of the two mills may bring them. The whole affair, whether it is so intended or not, seems to imply a suspicion on the part of the Japanese of bad faith on the part of British consular officials who have given their word as to the ownership of these mills. There is nothing more which the Japanese need know, and there is nothing more which the British authorities need give.

One is, of course, not so unreasonable as to suggest [that] the Japanese may not seize Chinese property of an [enemy] ... be transferred to a third-power ... burden of proof ...

关于英资纱厂的争端

日本当局与以W.C.戈默索尔（W. C. Gomersall）先生为首的两家英资棉纺厂业主之间的争端正引起广泛关注和兴趣，因为其结果可能对日本占领区及公海上所有外国财产产生深远影响。

这两家涉案纱厂最初注册为华商企业，在战事爆发后由戈默索尔先生代表的英方利益集团购买。随后，日军奉命接管了这些纱厂，据称业主指派看护房产的某些成员在被逮捕的威胁下被驱逐。

英方业主召开了特别会议，其董事们表达了极大的愤慨。已通过英国驻沪总领事馆采取官方行动，旨在将财产归还给其合法所有者，但迄今为止，日本当局认为不宜接受英国的要求。

日本军方起初采取的立场基于去年九月发布的一份公告，其中规定，战事爆发后华人与外籍人士之间达成的任何形式的财产交易，无论是真实的还是虚构的，日本当局均不予承认。

正如本刊此前指出的那样，这种立场过于片面，在国际法或国际惯例中站不住脚。两国之间的军事敌对行动并不排除任一国国民与第三国国民进行贸易的可能性，当然，前提是此类贸易不包括违禁品。

事实上，敌对行动的持续必然为以低价购买财产提供绝佳机会，这纯粹是良好的商业行为。

在中国，这一原则因以下事实而得到进一步加强：除少数例外，外籍人士已将其大部分财产集中在公共租界和法租界内，这两个区域凭借其国际或外籍性质而免受战争影响。在这两个区域内，中国人和日本人可以自由居住和贸易，因此其他外籍人士必然享有同样的特权，可以与中国人或日本人进行正常的贸易和商业活动。

日本所持立场的谬误似乎已给日本领事官员留下了深刻印象。因此，据报道，与此争端有关的日本发言人表示，纱厂在战事爆发后转让这一事实属于“次要问题”。

日本现在坚持的唯一一点是涉案两家纱厂确属英国所有。虽然证明所有权看似简单，但在这种情况下实际上非常困难。

日本方面要求的所有权证明可能远超法院通常要求的范围。英国业主已为此向英国驻沪总领事馆提交了所有文件，该馆又将其提交给日本驻沪总领事馆，最后提交给日本军事指挥官。

英国业主的态度是，英国驻沪总领事馆出具的英国所有权官方认证应已足够，而日本方面显然要求的不只是英国的官方登记。

虽然可以承认，并非所有的官方登记文件都是真实所有权的绝对证明，因为即使是官员也可能无意中犯错或轻信，但国际礼让要求一国代表在正常事态下接受另一国代表的官方声明。如果每个国家都可以随心所欲地要求在官方认证之外提供最细微的私有财产细节，世界确实会变成令人难以置信的怪诞景象。仅在上海，如果日本当局不依靠其他列强官员的诚信，而是自行承担证明或反驳外国财产所有权的任务，他们将忙得不可开交。国际礼让不仅是外交礼节的问题，也是数个世纪艰苦经验的结果。

如果当前的争端不及时解决，由此产生的麻烦可能在善意和商业方面给日本带来的损失，超过保留这两家纱厂所带来的收益。整件事，无论是否有意为之，似乎暗示日本方面怀疑已就这些纱厂所有权作出保证的英国领事官员缺乏诚意。日本方面无需知晓更多，英国当局也无需提供更多。

当然，人们不会如此不讲理地建议[说]日本人不得没收[敌方]的中国财产……转让给第三强国……举证责任……

01642

Shareholders Of China Textile Manufacturing Co.,
And China Spinners, Ltd., Vote To Make
Formal Representation To Authorities

NO VALID REASON FOR OCCUPATION
OF WORKS BY TOYODA MILL

The shareholders of the China Textile Manufacturing Company, Limited and the China Spinners, Limited, both companies incorporated under the Companies' Ordinances of Hongkong, held extraordinary meetings yesterday and passed resolutions protesting against the occupation of their cotton mill by the Toyoda Mill, despite the fact that the companies represent genuine and substantial British interests.

It was also decided to make representations through H.B.M. Consulate-General with a view to obtaining the release of the mill and its restoration with all its property to the company. Shareholders of nationalities other than British were requested at the meeting to make the necessary representations to protect their interests through their respective national authorities.

The first meeting to be called was that of shareholders of the China Spinners Limited. Both metings were held at 88 Museum Road. Mr. W. C. Gomersall, Managing Director, presided, supported by Mr. E. S. Elliston, Mr. K. S. Ging, and Mr. K. G. Stephenson, Directors, with the following shareholders being present: Sir Robert Calder Marshall, Messrs. F. A. Garcia, J. R. Jones, F. L. Sable, E. Schuster, F. R. Smith and George F. Richardson (on behalf of Mr. C. V. Starr), representing 9,355 shares.

Having read the notice convening the meeting, the Chairman said:—
"When we decided to form ourselves into a Company to purchase the Chun Tah Cotton Mill we were in peaceful possession of the property. The hostilities as you know, broke out in August. The Japanese occupied the district in November. We signed our preliminary Deed of Sale in September, and we obtained our Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of Companies on December 1, 1937.
"There were two British members of our staff resident at the mill up to December 21. About that time, the local Japanese Military Officer informed us that he had ascertained that the mill was formerly Chinese property, and that we had no right to fly the British flag. He ordered the withdrawal of our staff from the mill, otherwise he would have them arrested. We pointed out that for many years there have been important foreign interests in the mill, that, for example, the land was British-owned, that various foreign firms had supplied machinery on deferred terms, and had installed plant to supply the mills with power and steam. We showed him our machinery contracts, our British Title Deeds, and our Certificate of Incorporation. His reply was that the mill had been sold after the outbreak of hostilities, and the Japanese could not recognize any sales after that time. Our arguments were unavailing, and we had to withdraw our men, or run the risk of an "incident." The British flag was taken down, and the Japanese flag put up in its place.

presents genuine and substantial British interests that representations be made through H.B.M. Consulate-General in Shanghai with the view of obtaining the release of the mill and its restoration with all its property to the company and that shareholders of nationalities other than British be requested to make the necessary representations to protect their interests through their respective national authorities."

Sir Robert Calder Marshall.—I second the resolution.
Before asking you to pass the resolution the meeting is open for discussion.

Sir Robert Calder Marshall.—I would like to ask whether you have made it quite clear to the Japanese Authorities that the Mill is private property?

Mr. Gomersall.—Yes, that has been made very clear. In October, some time before the Japanese occupied the district, we wrote to the British Consul advising him that there were British interests in this Mill. He requested us to call at the Consulate, and prove that British interests were involved, and after we had done that, he wrote to the Japanese Consul-General. I saw the letter in the Japanese Consulate. Subsequently I called on the Japanese Army Officer in charge of the Mill district, as well as on the Japanese Consulate, and clearly explained the relation between the Chinese and foreign interests. Both of them said that we were shielding the Chinese. I replied that their own Mills, such as the Shanghai Cotton Mills, had Chinese Shareholders; and in defending our own rights, it was inevitable that the Chinese would be protected too. That arose from applying the principle of foreign and Chinese co-operation.

Mr. G. F. Richardson.—I am here to represent Mr. C. V. Starr, who, unfortunately, had to leave last Wednesday for Hongkong. He particularly requested me to express his regrets that he was not able to be present at this important meeting. On his behalf, I would like to ask, what is the condition of the Mill? Could it be started up at once? It is reported that some mills have been damaged maliciously.

就日军占领英国财产提出正式抗议

01642

中国纺织制造有限公司及中国纺纱有限公司股东投票决定向当局提出正式交涉

丰田纱厂占领工厂并无正当理由

中国纺织制造有限公司（China Textile Manufacturing Company, Limited）与中国纺纱有限公司（China Spinners, Limited）的股东于昨日举行特别会议，这两家公司均依据香港《公司条例》注册。会议通过决议，抗议丰田纱厂（Toyoda Mill）占领其棉纺厂，尽管这两家公司代表着真实且重大的英国利益。

会议还决定通过英国驻华总领事馆进行交涉，以期收回该厂并将其所有财产归还公司。会议请非英籍股东通过各自国籍的主管当局进行必要的交涉，以保护其利益。

首先召开的是中国纺纱有限公司的股东会议。两次会议均在博物馆路88号举行。总经理 W. C. Gomersall 先生主持会议，董事 E. S. Elliston 先生、K. S. Ging 先生和 K. G. Stephenson 先生予以协助，出席的股东如下：Robert Calder Marshall 爵士，F. A. Garcia 先生、J. R. Jones 先生、F. L. Sable 先生、E. Schuster 先生、F. R. Smith 先生以及 George F. Richardson 先生（代表 C. V. Starr 先生），共代表股份9,355股。

主席宣读召集会议的通知后说道：——
“当我们决定组建公司购买纯大棉纺厂（Chun Tah Cotton Mill）时，我们和平地占有着该财产。众所周知，战事于八月爆发。日军于十一月占领了该地区。我们于九月签署了初步卖契，并于1937年12月1日从公司注册处获得了公司注册证书。
“直到12月21日，我们有两名英籍职员居住在厂内。大约在那时，当地日本军官通知我们，他已查明该厂原为中国财产，我们无权悬挂英国国旗。他命令我们的职员撤离工厂，否则将逮捕他们。我们指出，多年来该厂一直有重要的外国利益存在，例如，土地为英人所有，各家外国商行以延期付款的方式提供机器，并安装设备为工厂提供电力和蒸汽。我们向他展示了我们的机器合同、英国地契以及公司注册证书。他的回答是，该厂是在战事爆发后出售的，日本人不承认此后的任何买卖。我们的争辩无效，我们不得不撤出人员，以免发生‘事件’。英国国旗被降下，取而代之的是日本国旗。

鉴于本厂代表着真实且重大的英国利益，兹决定通过驻上海的英国总领事馆进行交涉，以期收回该厂并将其所有财产归还公司；并请非英籍股东通过各自国籍的主管当局进行必要的交涉，以保护其利益。”

Robert Calder Marshall 爵士：——我附议该决议。
在提请你们通过决议之前，会议开放讨论。

Robert Calder Marshall 爵士：——我想请问，你们是否已向日本当局明确说明该厂是私有财产？

Gomersall 先生：——是的，这一点已经非常清楚。在十月，即日军占领该地区之前的一段时间，我们致函英国领事，告知他该厂涉及英国利益。他要求我们前往领事馆，证明涉及英国利益，在我们这样做之后，他致函日本总领事。我在日本领事馆看到了这封信。随后，我拜访了负责该厂地区的日本陆军军官以及日本领事馆，清楚地解释了中方与外方利益之间的关系。他们两人都说我们在庇护中国人。我回答说，他们自己的工厂，如上海棉纺厂（Shanghai Cotton Mills），也有中国股东；在维护我们自身权利的同时，保护中国人也是不可避免的。这是应用中外合作原则的结果。

G. F. Richardson 先生：——我在此代表 C. V. Starr 先生，他不幸已于上周三前往香港。他特别请求我表达他对未能出席这次重要会议的遗憾。我代表他请问，工厂的现状如何？能否立即开工？据报道，有些工厂遭到了恶意破坏。

"There appears to be no valid
reason why the mill should not be
operated. Our workers could be
ferried across the Creek in a few
minutes without any possible in-
terference with Japanese Military
movements. Had we been per-
mitted to work the mill within the
last few months it would have been
possible to realize good profits, as
the market for our products has
been exceptionally favourable.

Publicity Sought

"Your Directors are of the opinion
that the only way to obtain redress
is to give the matter wide public-
ity. The Japanese contention that
that they do not recognize our
purchase of these mills is equivalent
to an embargo on all business
transactions. If Third Power par-
ties are prepared to accept such an
edict it means that no business
transactions with Chinese can be
carried out without the consent of
the Japanese.
"In order that the views of our
shareholders in this matter may be
made known to the Japanese Au-
thorities as well as to our own
Authorities, I will now propose the
following resolution:—
Resolved that the Shareholders
of the China Spinners Ltd. in
general meeting assembled here-
by protest against the occupation
of our cotton mill by the Toyoda
Mill, and inasmuch as this mill
is owned by a company incor-
porated under the Companies'
Ordinances Hongkong and re-

Machinery Intact

Mr. Gomersall.—The machinery is
in perfect condition. Two members
of our foreign staff were at the mill
till December; and from December
to April we had six Chinese watch-
men there. These watchmen were
turned out by the Toyoda Mill when
they took possession in April.
Therefore, unless the mill has been
damaged by the Toyoda people,
which is unlikely, it is still in good
condition, and able to start up at
short notice. This also disposes of
any possibility of malicious damage.
Mr. F. R. Smith.—What support
are you receiving from H M. Consul-
General?
Mr. Gomersall.—He is doing his
best and has little doubt that even-
tually the mills will have to be re-
stored to us.
Mr. E. Schuster.—I am glad to
note that the resolution includes a
request for Shareholders, other than
British, to protest through their res-
pective Consulates. As a matter of
fact, I have already sent a protest
to my Consulate, and I hope our
American and Portuguese friends
will do the same.
Mr. Gomersall.—I am sure that
they will.
Sir Robert Calder Marshall.—It
would appear from conversations I
have had with Japanese officials,
that there is no intention on the part
of the Japanese Government either
to confiscate the Mills or to insist
on compulsory co-operation; and in
view of the numerous assurances
that have been given that property
of private citizens will not be inter-
fered with, and that foreign inter-
ests will be respected, thus ob-
viously the Toyoda Mill have no
legal or moral right to occupy the
property.
The Chairman then put the ques-
tion to the meeting, and the resolu-
tion was carried unanimously.
Immediately following this meet-
ing there was a meeting of Share-
holders of the China Textile Manu-
facturing Co., Ltd. and a similar
resolution was passed.

Ownership Of
British Mills
Proved Genuine

Nippon Army Action
Said Taken Without
Any Investigations

"Bona-fide British ownership of
the mills involved have already
been proved to and accepted by
H. B. M. Consul-General in Shang-
hai," declared Mr. W. C. Gomersall
yesterday afternoon when shown a
release by the Japanese official
spokesman to the effect that this
factor would be the principal ele-
ment to be studied when the matter
came up for consideration by the
Japanese authorities.
"Whether the transactions were
'specious or genuine' was made
perfectly clear by the Chairman's
report at the protest meetings,
where it was stated that all the
documents in proof of British in-
terests in the two mills, the
Chun Tah Cotton Mill, and
the dyeing, printing and fini-
shing works of the China Textile
Manufacturing Company, had been
submitted to H. B. M. Consul-
General, to the Japanese Con-
sulate-General, and finally, to the
Japanese Military Commander.
"In spite of this, the Japanese
military authorities, without wait-
ing for an investigation, or for
proper representations through the
civil authorities, compelled the
British members of the mill staff
to leave the premises.
Transfer Genuine
"It is impossible to suppose that
anybody can really entertain any
doubt as to the genuineness of the
transfer from Chinese to British
ownership. Any doubts as to that
point could be set at rest in five
minutes by telephoning the British
Consulate-General, where China
Spinners, Limited, is registered.
"It is interesting to observe
that the spokesman states that
the fact that the sale was made
after the outbreak of hostilities
was of secondary importance. It
was the main reason given for the
compulsory withdrawal of the
British staff from the mill. This
is a welcome change from what all
third party nationals have always
regarded as an untenable position."
Sir Robert Calder-Marshall,
Chairman of the British Chamber
of Commerce, was equally emphatic.
"This amounts to the question of
whether Japanese have the right
to interfere with private property.
We have been assured again and
again that the Japanese have no
designs upon foreign property—
nor even on Chinese property. Yet
here we are confronted with the
seizure of British property, land
and machinery. The two facts do
not go well together."

Japanese Statement
Whether or not the transaction
involving the sale of the Chinese
Chun Tah Cotton Mill to the
British China Spinners Limited, a
company formed especially for this
purpose, was "specious or genuine"
would determine the attitude of the
Japanese authorities towards the
case, a Japanese Embassy spokes-
man said yesterday morning.
The bona fides of the deal, the
spokesman said, would be the
principal element to be studied.
The fact that the preliminary

01670

deed of sale had been signed in
September, after the outbreak of
the hostilities in Shanghai, was of
secondary importance, the spokes-
man indicated.
He declined to comment further
on the case, stating that an in-
vestigation into the case was now
being made by experts.

“涉事纱厂的 bona-fide（善意/真实）英国所有权已经向英国驻上海总领事证明并为其所接受，”W. C. Gomersall 先生昨日下午在见到日本官方发言人发布的一份声明后如是说，该声明称，当日本当局审议此事时，这一因素将是主要考量要素。
“交易是‘虚饰还是真实’，在抗议会议的主席报告中已阐述得十分清楚，报告指出，证明两家纱厂——纯大纱厂（Chun Tah Cotton Mill）以及中国纺织制造公司（China Textile Manufacturing Company）的印染整理厂——中英国利益的所有文件，均已提交给英国驻上海总领事、日本总领事馆，并最终提交给日本军事指挥官。
“尽管如此，日本军方当局未等待调查，也未通过民政当局进行适当交涉，便强迫纱厂职员中的英国人离开工厂 premises（厂区）。
转让属实
“任何人若对从中国所有权转让给英国所有权的真实性存疑，这种想法都是站不住脚的。关于这一点的任何疑虑，只需致电英国总领事馆即可在五分钟内消除，中国纺纱有限公司（China Spinners, Limited）即在该处注册。
“值得注意的是，发言人称，出售行为发生在敌对行动爆发之后，这一事实属于次要因素。而这正是此前强制英国职员撤出纱厂的主要理由。这与所有第三方国籍人士一直认为站不住脚的立场相比，是一个令人欢迎的转变。”
英国商会主席 Robert Calder-Marshall 爵士同样态度坚决。“这归结为日本人是否有权干涉私有财产的问题。我们一再得到保证，日本人对外国财产——甚至对中国财产——没有企图。然而，我们现在面对的是英国财产、土地和机器被扣押的事实。这两者难以自圆其说。”

日本大使馆发言人昨日上午表示，涉及将中国纯大纱厂出售给专为此次目的成立的英国公司中国纺纱有限公司的交易究竟是“虚饰还是真实”，将决定日本当局对此案的态度。

01796

Question Of Japanese Right
To Occupy Property

Matter Of British Interests In Shanghai Comes
Up Anew In Commons; Tariff Rates, British
Shipping Are Among Other Subjects

LONDON, July 21.—China and the situation in Shanghai were again brought up in various questions asked by members in the House of Commons yesterday.

Among the matters discussed were the alleged Japanese occupation of British property in Shanghai, the situation of the Shanghai Municipal Council in relation to the Hongkew and Yangtzepoo areas, the safety of British shipping on the Yangtze and the Tariff Autonomy Treaty signed by Great Britain and China in 1928.

In reply to a question asked by Sir John Wardlaw-Milne, Conservative member for the Kidderminster division of Worcestershire, Mr. R. A. Butler, Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, said that Viscount Halifax, Foreign Secretary, expected a report shortly regarding the Japanese occupation of the British-owned Moller Engineering Works, in Shanghai.

Sir Percy Harris, Liberal member for Southwest Bethnal Green, thereupon asked what legal right the Japanese had to take possession of British property, especially in Shanghai.

Mr. Butler answered that there were particular considerations regarding the Moller Works, which lay in a strategic area.

Tariff Autonomy Treaties

Mr. Harry Day, Labour member for Central Southwark, sought a statement on how the Autonomy and Tariff Treaties, signed by the British Government and the Chinese National Government, were working at present.

“As far as we are concerned,” Mr. Butler replied, “we continue to adhere to the principle of tariff autonomy for China as it has been laid down in the Tariff Autonomy Treaty of 1928.”

The Chinese Government, he declared, continued to apply the 1934 tariff duties to the areas they controlled, while in Japanese controlled areas the duty rates of 1931, with certain modifications, were applied.

Sir John Wardlaw-Milne then asked whether British shipping companies trading on the Yangtze would resume sailings either by convoy or other naval protection.

Mr. Butler replied that, as Viscount Halifax understood the position, shipping firms would be glad of convoys if they could take the ships through the Kiangyin Boom.

Turning again to Shanghai, Mr. Butler, in reply to a question asked by Commander Arthur Marsden, Conservative member for the Chertsey division of Surrey, said that no date had yet been fixed for the restoration of the Hongkew and Yangtzepoo districts to the Shanghai Municipal Council.

Further representations in the matter, he added, had been made in Tokyo on July 13.—Reuter.

Reported Informal Parleys

LONDON, July 20. — Japanese diplomatic circles here admitted today that informal negotiations on various problems were being carried on between Great Britain and Japan, although they considered as inaccurate information from Japanese sources according to which negotiations of a general character had opened in Tokyo between the Foreign Minister, General Ugaki, and H.B.M. Ambassador, Sir Robert L. Craigie.

Japanese diplomats stressed that, according to the reports reaching them, the talks being carried on between General Ugaki and Sir Robert were devoid of political character and there was no question whatever, for the time being at least, of British mediation in the present Far Eastern conflict.

The informal talks which are now pursued in Tokyo, the same circles declared, specially dealt with the following problems:

1.—Re-establishment of freedom of navigation on the Yangtze River.

2.—Restoration of competitive trade in Manchurian furs, it being recalled that this branch of activity has been practically monopolized by the Japanese, to the detriment of British traders.

3.—Collaboration with the local authorities in Japanese-controlled territories in China.

The most important of these problems—namely, that of the re-establishment of freedom of navigation on the Yangtze River—had already been discussed between the two countries, but the parleys were interrupted in May last.

Japanese circles here considered that the most serious of these local problems was that of British properties in China which have been fortified by the Chinese and have become military objectives for the Japanese forces. A new protest on that issue was forwarded yesterday to Hankow by Sir Archibald Clark Kerr, Japanese diplomats here alleged.—Havas.

01796

日本占领财产的权利问题

上海英国利益事项再次在下议院提出；关税税率、英国航运等为其他议题

伦敦，7月21日。—昨日，下议院议员提出的各种问题中，再次提及中国及上海局势。

讨论的事项包括：据称日本占领上海英国财产、工部局在虹口和杨树浦地区的处境、英国船只在长江的安全，以及英国与中国于1928年签署的关税自主条约。

在回答伍斯特郡基德明斯特选区保守党议员 John Wardlaw-Milne 爵士的提问时，外交部次官 R. A. Butler 先生表示，外交大臣哈利法克斯子爵（Viscount Halifax）预计不久将收到关于日本占领上海英商茂生机器工程公司（Moller Engineering Works）的报告。

随后，西南贝思纳尔格林选区自由党议员 Percy Harris 爵士询问，日本有何法律依据占有英国财产，尤其是在上海。

Butler 先生回答说，茂生机器厂位于战略区域，因此存在特殊的考量因素。

关税自主条约

南华克中心选区工党议员 Harry Day 先生要求就英国政府与中国国民政府签署的自主与关税条约目前的执行情况发表声明。

“就我方而言，”Butler 先生回答，“我们继续坚持1928年《关税自主条约》中规定的中国关税自主原则。”

他宣称，中国政府继续在其控制地区适用1934年的关税税率，而在日本控制地区，则适用经某些修改的1931年税率。

John Wardlaw-Milne 爵士随后询问，在长江经营的英国航运公司是否会恢复航行，无论是通过护航还是其他海军保护。

Butler 先生回答说，据哈利法克斯子爵了解的情况，如果航运公司能让船只通过江阴封锁线（Kiangyin Boom），他们将乐意接受护航。

再次回到上海话题，Butler 先生在回答萨里郡切特西选区保守党议员 Arthur Marsden 指挥官的提问时表示，尚未确定将虹口和杨树浦地区归还工部局的日期。

他补充说，7月13日已在东京就此事进行了进一步交涉。—路透社。

据报道的非正式会谈

伦敦，7月20日。—此间日本外交界今日承认，英国与日本正在就各种问题进行非正式谈判，尽管他们认为来自日本方面的消息不准确，该消息称外交大臣宇垣一成将军（General Ugaki）与英国大使 Robert L. Craigie 爵士已在东京开启了总体性质的谈判。

日本外交官强调，根据他们收到的报告，宇垣将军与 Robert 爵士之间的谈话不具有政治性质，至少目前不存在英国调解当前远东冲突的问题。

同一圈子的人士宣称，目前在东京进行的非正式谈话特别涉及以下问题：

1.—恢复长江航行自由。

2.—恢复满洲皮货的竞争性贸易，需指出的是，该行业实际上已被日本垄断，损害了英国商人的利益。

3.—与中国日本控制区的地方当局合作。

这些问题中最重要的一个——即恢复长江航行自由——两国此前已进行过讨论，但会谈于去年五月中断。

此间日本圈子认为，这些地方问题中最严重的是在华英国财产问题，这些财产已被中方设防，并成为日军的军事目标。据此处日本外交官称，Archibald Clark Kerr 爵士昨日已就此事向汉口发出新的抗议。—哈瓦斯社。

Japanese Factories Opening
In Occupied Territory

Question Is Asked In Commons; British Factories
Are Still Prohibited From Working; Basic
Rail Shares Said In Japan's Hands

LONDON, July 12.—"On what grounds does the Japanese Government justify the opening of Japanese factories in occupied areas inside and outside the International Settlement, while prohibiting the working of foreign-owned factories on the ground of military necessity?" asked Mr. Adrian Moreing, Conservative member for Preston, in the House of Commons yesterday.

Mr. R. A. Butler, Under-Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, stated in reply that although the Japanese Government had hitherto made no pronouncement on the subject, it was understood that they maintained that control could be exercised over Chinese workmen in Japanese factories.

They were not, however, satisfied in all cases that control sufficient to prevent subversive activities could be exercised over Chinese workmen in foreign factories.

The matter, Mr. Butler said, was still under discussion both in Shanghai and in Tokyo.

Question Of Shares

Mr. Ian Hannah, National Government member for the Bilston Division of Wolverhampton, drew attention to the fact that the Japanese Government had presented the basic shares in the railways of North and Central China to Japanese charter companies.

The value of these shares, he said, totalled 38,000,000 yen.

Mr. Hannah urged that a protest should be made against such action on the part of the Japanese Government, as "such shares have priority over British capital invested in these lines."

Mr. Butler stated in reply that charter companies could not be formed until October, and quoted a Japanese press report that the draft Articles of Association provide that the Japanese Government subscribe 175,000,000 yen and 50,000,000 yen, half the total of capitalization of the North China and Central China companies respectively, and from these amounts 30,500,000 yen for the Central China company would be in the form of railway rolling stock.—Reuter.

日本工厂在占领区开业

下议院提出质询；英国工厂仍被禁止开工；基本铁路股据说落入日本手中

伦敦，7月12日。—“日本政府以何种理由证明其在国际租界内外占领区开设日本工厂的正当性，同时却以军事需要为由禁止外资工厂开工？”普雷斯顿选区保守党议员 Adrian Moreing 先生昨日在下议院问道。

外交部次官 R. A. Butler 先生在答复中表示，虽然日本政府迄今未就此发表声明，但据了解，他们维持这样的观点：可以对日本工厂中的中国工人实施控制。

然而，他们并非在所有情况下都确信，能够对外国工厂中的中国工人实施足以防止颠覆活动的控制。

Butler 先生说，此事仍在上海和东京进行讨论。

股份问题

伍尔弗汉普顿比尔斯顿选区国民政府议员 Ian Hannah 先生提请注意这样一个事实：日本政府已将华北和华中铁路上路的基本股份移交给日本特许公司。

他说，这些股份的价值总计为38,000,000日元。

Hannah 先生敦促应对日本政府的此类行为提出抗议，因为“这些股份优先于投入这些线路的英国资本。”

Butler 先生在答复中表示，特许公司在十月之前无法成立，并引用日本报刊报道说，公司章程草案规定，日本政府分别认购华北和华中公司资本总额的一半，即175,000,000日元和50,000,000日元，其中用于华中公司的30,500,000日元将以铁路机车车辆的形式出资。—路透社。

definitely better than it was last July.

the British authorities making an in-

The China Engineers Limited proceed-

据昨日在博物馆路88号举行的该厂业主中国纺织有限公司（China Spinners Ltd.）第二次年度会议上报告，位于圣约翰大学附近苏州河畔的纯大纱厂（Chun Tah cotton mill）于1937年12月间某时被驻沪日军占领，随后被移交给日本丰田棉纺厂（Toyoda Cotton mill），目前仍处于日方控制之下。然而，董事长报告称，局势较去年有所好转，因为日本当局已承认其中涉及重大的英国及外国利益，并允许英国当局对工厂进行检查，以查明财产状况。
W. C. Gomersall 先生（董事长兼总经理）主持会议，E. S. Elliston 先生、K. G. Stephenson 先生、C. Y. Wong 先生和 C. Y. Chiang 先生列席支持。出席会议代表的股份总数为9,115股。
董事长在发言中说：“资产负债表已在各位手中数日，经各位允许，我将视为已宣读。由于工厂未开工，故无损益账目可示。我很遗憾地通知各位，工厂尚未归还我方。各位应记得，这些工厂于1937年12月间某时被日本军方占领，随后被移交给日本丰田棉纺厂。
确实有所好转
1938年7月，曾召开股东特别会议，正式向各位通报情况，并请各位通过各自所属领事馆提出抗议。自那时以来，我们一直与英国当局保持联系；虽然我知道，作为股东，在看到工厂恢复并投入运转之前，你们不太可能感到满意，但鉴于我们的处境确实比去年7月时有所好转，或许能令各位稍感宽慰。日方已承认其中涉及重大的英国及外国利益，鉴于这一事实，他们同意英国当局对工厂进行检查，以查明财产状况。因此，去年12月9日，由英国驻华总监事 A. G. N. Ogden 先生、负责日本事务的英国领事 H. H. Thomas 先生组成的代表团，在日本总领事馆的 A. Umekawa 先生和中国工程有限公司（The China Engineers Limited）的 J. W. Brierley 先生的陪同下，前往工厂进行了彻底检查。
上周市场上传出谣言，称我们存放在仓库中的棉花以及工厂内的部分机器已被搬走。英国驻华
会议上一致通过。随后由 J. R. Jones 先生提议，F. R. Smith 先生附议，一致通过重新选举 E. S. Elliston 先生和 C. Y. Wong 先生为董事。由 E. Schuster 先生提议，George Richardson 先生附议，一致通过重新选举 Thomson & Company 为审计师。
同样处于日方控制之下
在中国纺织有限公司会议结束后，举行了中国纺织制造股份有限公司（China Textile Manufacturing Company, Ltd.）的年度会议。
Gomersall 先生说：“我刚才就中国纺织有限公司所作的评论，同样适用于中国纺织制造股份有限公司。我们在曹家渡（Tsaokadoo）的主要工厂仍控制在日方手中，且全年停工。然而，我们在延平路有一处小型临时工厂，已运营七个月，因此我们得以实现利润59,003.71美元。各位董事现已决定将该工厂基本固定下来，目前正在对其进行全面的重组和扩建，预计在下一次会议之前很久即可完工。
各位董事无法建议派发股息，这并不令各位惊讶。关于处置59,003.71美元款项的建议如下：
注销所有开办费用 .................... 9,463.52美元
支付董事酬金 ......... 2,500.00美元
结转至新账户 ...................... 47,040.17美元
总计 ...................... 59,003.71美元
我现在提议通过董事报告及1938年度账目。此动议由 K. G. Stephenson 先生附议，但在提交会议表决前，我将尝试回答任何问题。
该决议提交会议并获一致通过。
E. S. Elliston 先生和 C. Y. Wong 先生再次当选为董事会成员，Thomson & Company 再次当选为审计师。
